_comment: The Grade 4 Art & Design standalone lesson build, described for ../../mathematics/lesson-app-tools and built by ../lesson-kit. Order here IS the lesson number. Eight lessons against Cambridge Primary Art & Design 0067 Stage 4. Cambridge writes ONE progression text for Stages 3 and 4 together, word for word the same, so Grade 4 steps up by CONTENT, the way Grade 2 did from Grade 1 (see README.md :: The Stage 3 / Stage 4 line): it takes the parts of that text Grade 3 left - the print that becomes a collaborative textile, the parts of a model that come under stress, the photographic diary of a build, pen marks layered over a painting, comparing one subject across times and cultures, and reviewing work together as a group. Progress is written under u01..u08 beneath ehel-art-g04, whose catalogue entry is generated FROM this lesson list. objectiveFloors are recorded at the measured value after each build and may rise, not fall.
subject: art-and-design

Its review lessons are Grade 3's, linked in ../grade-3-v2/. It is not a lesson and reports nothing to the gradebook.
hubStrands: Looking at a street and finding why the far end is small; looking closely at a cloth printed from a carved block, a jar painted in bands, a cast metal head and a wall painting from long ago; and asking what each artist used and who they made it for.

Drawing what is really in front of us, with guide lines and measured sizes; mixing a colour until it matches; printing in two colours that line up; building a pot from coils and slabs; making a model stand up; and adding pen, paper and marks on top of a painting.

Judging our work against what it was for; giving a friend praise AND one piece of guidance; saying how another artist's work moved our own work on; and hanging an exhibition so other people can read it.

Showing that one idea can be made in more than one way; keeping a photo diary of a build and using it the next time; printing one tile that joins a whole class cloth; and getting a show ready together.
